correctness.rationale: For each forced opposite-part path, the rooted-forest Laplacian minor is an explicit two-block determinant. Requiring specified additional endpoint neighbors gives exact factorial moments, factoring into a binomial plus an exceptional Bernoulli. Adjacent Bernoulli convolutions are log-concave, yielding strict likelihood-ratio comparisons. The conditional mean has a monotone cubic sign factor and the distance tail is an exact product giving the Rayleigh limit. The included checker independently matched 47,930 exact assertions, and a larger rational sweep matched 1,566,873 likelihood-ratio cross-products; the analytic proof handles all integer parameters.

originality.rationale: The new assessed statement is strict all-parameter likelihood-ratio decay of an endpoint degree conditional on opposite-part distance and a unique mean-bias crossing on the Rayleigh distance scale. Prior complete-bipartite fixed-tree and forest enumeration theorems do supply the basic containment counts, which are expressly not claimed to be new. The inspected sections do not state the conditional order or crossover, and a related complete-graph result concerns a different host and only stochastic order. Priority risk from unindexed literature and general enumeration consequences is retained.
residual_risks: Generic fixed-tree inclusion identities make the conditional mass formula derivable from earlier work, so originality is confined to the qualitative likelihood-ratio comparison and Rayleigh-scale threshold.
An indexed related complete-graph endpoint-distance result was available only by abstract rather than inspected full text; it does not itself establish the bipartite claim by its stated scope.
Broader historic probability literature might contain equivalent reverse-TP2 or monotone-regression statements under different terminology.
